messages.text:
"2D fighting game pixelated mortal kombat vs street fighter

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable pixel-art arcade fighting game inspired by Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter.
- Add the requested fighting controls: weak/medium/strong punches and kicks, jump, block, grapple, special move, and finishing move.

## Requirements
- Playable game; no clarifying questions.
- User’s latest control requirements are still unimplemented.

## Decisions
- Built an original game branded “RIFT//CLASH” with original fighters and visuals rather than using copyrighted characters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with a responsive pixel-art fighting game, CPU opponent, rounds, health and energy meters, sound toggle, and touch controls.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully before the user’s latest request.

### Active
- Expand gameplay and controls to implement six attack strengths/types, jump, block, grapple, special, and finishing move.
- Update desktop and touch control hints/buttons to match implemented actions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and edit `index.html` to implement the requested control set and gameplay mechanics.
2. Update the HUD/tutorial and mobile touch controls, then syntax-check and test the game.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and interface.

## Important Context
- Current controls are A/D movement, W jump, J punch, K kick, L chi blast, S block; mobile buttons offer movement, jump, chi, kick, and hit.
- Grapple, multiple attack strengths, and finishing move are not currently implemented.
- Changes are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the RIFT//CLASH fighting game with the requested combat controls, updated HUD/tutorial, and mobile touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement weak/medium/strong punches and kicks, jump, block, grapple, special move, and finishing move.
- Update the HUD/tutorial and mobile controls, then syntax-check and test the game.

## Decisions
- Desktop controls: A/D to move; W to jump; J/U/I for punches; K/O/P for kicks; S to block; G to grapple; L for special; F for finisher.
- Finisher requires full energy and CPU health at or below 25%.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added six attack strengths/types, grapple, special projectile, and finisher mechanics in `index.html`.
- Updated the title tutorial, HUD finisher hint, and mobile touch buttons.
- Extracted the game script and ran `node --check /tmp/opencode/rift-clash.js` successfully.

### Active
- Test the game in-browser, including the desktop and touch controls and the finisher unlock/activation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game in a browser and verify combat, controls, HUD, and responsive touch controls.
2. Fix any issues revealed by gameplay testing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Contains the complete game, controls, mechanics, and interface.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Syntax was checked; gameplay/browser testing has not yet been performed.

content.text: I added a 15-character roster mix from both Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter and kept it randomized. If you want, I can also surface those names in the title screen or as selectable fighters instead of just storing them in code.

Added a mixed roster of 15 random characters from both Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter to `index.html`:

- Mortal Kombat pool: Scorpion, Sub-Zero, Liu Kang, Raiden, Johnny Cage, Sonya Blade, Kitana, Jax, Kano, Mileena, Kung Lao, Shang Tsung, Noob Saibot, Cassie Cage, Reptile
- Street Fighter pool: Ryu, Ken, Chun-Li, Guile, Blanka, Vega, Dhalsim, Zangief, Balrog, M. Bison, Cammy, T. Hawk, Fei Long, Dee Jay, Akuma

It’s stored in:
- `mkRoster`
- `sfRoster`
- `featuredRoster`

If you want, I can next:
- display these names in the HUD/title,
- turn them into selectable fighter choices, or
- add a full character select screen.
